Blend: The team's overall rating, in percent better or worse than an average team (offense minus defense plus special teams). Early in the season it mixes this season's play with a starting estimate taken from last season's final rating. The starting estimate's weight falls with each game the team plays and reaches zero at its 13th game.

Model Line: The model gives 0.334 points of margin for each point of Blend difference between the two teams, plus 2.25 points to the home team (none at a neutral site). So a team 10 points of Blend better than its opponent, at home, is favored by 5.6. Model Total comes from the two offenses and the two defenses, and the two Model scores split it by the Model Line.

Model Line and Spread: The points the favorite lays, shown in that team's row. PK = pick'em.

Edge: The model's margin for the market favorite minus the points it lays. Positive (green) means the model likes the favorite at that number; negative (red) means the model has the favorite winning by less than the spread, or losing.

O/U Edge: Model Total minus O/U. Positive (green) means the model total is above the market total; negative (red) means below.

Final: Each team's final score; empty until the game is final.

ATS: The spread pick's result in the row of the team the model picked against the closing spread: W (green) won, L (red) lost, P push. No pick when the model's margin equals the spread.

O/U Result: The total pick's result, in the home row: over when O/U Edge is positive, under when it is negative. W, L or P as for ATS.

Blend: The team's overall rating, in percent better or worse than an average team (offense minus defense plus special teams). Early in the season it mixes this season's play with a starting estimate taken from last season's final rating. The starting estimate's weight falls with each game the team plays and reaches zero at its 13th game.

Model Line: The model gives 0.334 points of margin for each point of Blend difference between the two teams, plus 2.25 points to the home team (none at a neutral site). So a team 10 points of Blend better than its opponent, at home, is favored by 5.6. Model Total comes from the two offenses and the two defenses, and the two Model scores split it by the Model Line.

Model Line and Spread: The points the favorite lays, shown in that team's row. PK = pick'em.

Edge: The model's margin for the market favorite minus the points it lays. Positive (green) means the model likes the favorite at that number; negative (red) means the model has the favorite winning by less than the spread, or losing.

O/U Edge: Model Total minus O/U. Positive (green) means the model total is above the market total; negative (red) means below.

Final: Each team's final score; empty until the game is final.

ATS: The spread pick's result in the row of the team the model picked against the closing spread: W (green) won, L (red) lost, P push. No pick when the model's margin equals the spread.

O/U Result: The total pick's result, in the home row: over when O/U Edge is positive, under when it is negative. W, L or P as for ATS.

How to read this

  1. A pick is made on every game with a closing line. Against the spread, the pick is the side the model's margin favors against the closing spread. On the total, the pick is over when the Model Total is above the closing total and under when it is below.
  2. Records are wins-losses-pushes. A push is a tie against the number. It is neither a win nor a loss and is left out of the percentages.
  3. “All” counts every pick. “Edge 3+” counts only picks where the model and the closing number differ by 3 points or more.
  4. Lines here are closing lines. The coming week's game tables above show the Spread and O/U available when this page was made, and they can move before kickoff; past weeks on the Week list show closing lines, like this scorecard. So a pick graded here can differ from the Edge the page showed that week.
  5. Backfilled weeks (1 to 4) were played before this model was finished. Their projections were rebuilt afterwards, each from only the games played before that week, the same way a live week's are. Live weeks (5 on) were projected before their games.
  6. At the usual −110 price, a bettor needs 52.4% to break even. The ± after each percentage is one standard error. Over a full 272-game season it is about 3 points, so one season's record is a small sample.
  7. Week 1 is projected from the prior alone: last season's ratings, before any game of this season. Weeks 2+ counts every graded pick from week 2 on, the weeks projected from this season's games.

How to read the two views

Success rate counts plays: the share that gained expected points. EPA/play weighs them, so turnovers and long gains count for more. A team ahead on success rate but behind on EPA lost on a few big plays. A team ahead on EPA but behind on success rate won on them. The helmet on top is the winner, and the bar is the winner's margin.

Blend: The team's overall rating, in percent better or worse than an average team (offense minus defense plus special teams). Early in the season it mixes this season's play with a starting estimate taken from last season's final rating. The starting estimate's weight falls with each game the team plays and reaches zero at its 13th game.

Ratings are percent better or worse than a league-average play in the same situation. Offense and special teams are better when positive; defense is better when negative. Total = Off - Def + ST.

Adj VOA is adjusted for opponents. Blend mixes it with the preseason prior by games played (SPEC 12.2). Weighted counts recent games more. Unadj VOA has no opponent adjustment.
